I'm ready to play Monopoly as an AI player.

I'm p4 with $192 and the full yellow set. I just paid $18 rent to p2. p1 has $478, all four railroads, and a mortgaged Boardwalk. I own the orange block that p1 needs to complete.

p2 has $466, GOOJF, and the pink and red blocks. p3 has $1958 with a light blue monopoly and three hotels. The bank holds 32 houses and 9 hotels. I can afford exactly one yellow house for $150, leaving $42.

One house leaves too little cash against p3's light blue hotels. Expected rent is low and the next roll from Indiana Avenue carries risk. I'm checking which players can land on my yellows before my next turn.

I'm mapping the standard board order to identify which players can land on my yellows before my next turn. I'm checking which spaces are dangerous from Indiana Avenue.

A roll of 3 from Indiana Avenue lands on B&O Railroad, costing $200. I cannot pay that with $192. Building a house would leave only $42 and guarantee bankruptcy if that happens.

Mortgaging my yellows would only raise about $580 total. That still falls short of the $200 B&O Railroad debt. If I build a house first, selling it for $75 leaves a net loss of $75 before mortgaging is even possible.

Mortgaging Park Place alone covers the $200 B&O Railroad debt, leaving about $167. Building a house first would leave only $42, forcing a house sale for $75 and still leaving an $83 shortfall. Even after mortgaging Park Place, cash would drop to roughly $92.

I am now uncertain which Community Chest p1 occupies. That position determines whether p1 can land on my yellows before my next turn.

From Kentucky Avenue, p2 can reach Indiana, Illinois, or B&O Railroad.

From Kentucky Avenue, p2 can land on my yellows with a 14 in 36 chance. That yields roughly $9 in expected rent if I have no houses. I must build evenly across the three yellows.

Building one house on Marvin Gardens yields the highest extra expected value at roughly $13.30. Ventnor follows at about $12.20, and Atlantic at about $9.80. p3 can land on my yellows from Illinois with a 10 in 36 chance, which would add roughly $13.30 to my income if I have one house on Marvin.

If p1 is on Community Chest 2, he can reach my yellows from there. He lands on Atlantic Avenue with a 3 in 36 chance and Ventnor Avenue with a 2 in 36 chance. Marvin Gardens is unreachable from that space. The extra expected value would be roughly $7.30 for Atlantic and $4.90 for Ventnor.

Community Chest 3 is too far from the yellows to threaten them. The combined extra expected value from one house on Marvin Gardens is roughly $27 to $34. That exceeds the $150 cost, so building is profitable.

I am now weighing the expected rent against the risk of having to sell a house at half price. The B&O Railroad hit remains the main danger, but I am also checking whether the Water Works utility could force a sale if I build first and land there with only $42 left.

Rolling a 6 from Indiana Avenue lands on Water Works for $60, which is unaffordable with only $42 left. Rolling a 2 hits Illinois for $24, leaving $18. Rolling a 3 hits B&O Railroad for $200, which is impossible to pay with either cash amount. Rolling a 10 lands on North Carolina, which costs $300 and is unaffordable.

Rolling a 12 from Indiana Avenue lands on Pennsylvania, which costs $28. That is affordable with either cash amount.

With $192, a roll of 3 leaves about $167 after paying the B&O Railroad debt. A roll of 6 leaves about $132 after paying Water Works. Both are manageable.

With only $42 left after building one house, a roll of 2 leaves just $18. A roll of 3 would still force bankruptcy.

I realized I can mortgage Park Place or New York Avenue to raise cash without selling my yellow house. That house would remain on the board, so I would not lose its value.

Mortgaging Park Place would leave about $17 after paying the B&O Railroad debt, so building a house is safe. I am now calculating the exact expected rent from one house on Marvin Gardens.

I am now calculating the exact expected rent from one house on Marvin Gardens. p2 from Kentucky can reach it on a roll of 8, adding roughly $13.33 in extra rent. p3 from Illinois can reach it on a roll of 6 for the same gain. p1 cannot land on Marvin from Community Chest 1 or 3, but from Community Chest 2 he could reach it with a roll of 12.

The best-case extra expected value from one house on Marvin Gardens is roughly $29. That includes about $13.33 from p2, about $13.33 from p3, and about $2.67 if p1 lands there from Community Chest 2.

Building the house costs $150 but leaves a cash buffer of only $42. The risk of needing to mortgage properties has shifted: without the house, only a roll of 3 forces a mortgage; with the house, even a roll of 3 would require selling it.

A roll of 6 from Indiana Avenue would force a mortgage to pay Water Works. Mortgaging New York Avenue would leave about $82, while mortgaging Park Place would leave about $157. A roll of 9 on Pacific Avenue leaves only $16. A roll of 12 on Pennsylvania Avenue leaves just $14. Community Chest could bring a bill such as a doctor visit for $50. The expected value of roughly $29 from one house is real money, and p3 has $1958 so the extra rent will not hurt them.

One house is a poor investment because it does not threaten anyone and drains the cash buffer. Threatening requires three houses on the yellows, which costs $1350 and is impossible with only $192. I am now considering trading New York Avenue to p1, who desperately wants it to complete his orange monopoly.

I cannot give New York Avenue to p1. He would mortgage his four railroads for $400, add his $478 cash, and build three houses on the orange set immediately. That would create a second death set worth roughly $550 each. I also cannot give Park Place to p1, because he already holds Boardwalk.

I am now weighing what assets I could trade for to fund building. The yellow set is my only monopoly, so trading it away would eliminate my build path unless I acquire another set.

p2 cannot complete any set without p3's properties, so p3 will not help me. p3 holds light blue hotels and $1958, so they have no incentive to trade. They do not own yellow, and buying my yellows would be suicidal for them. I will not sell New York Avenue to p1.

I checked whether p2 could trade with me for cash and properties to fund the yellow houses. He only has $466, which is far below the $1350 needed for three houses on the set. I also verified the exact rent values for each house level on the yellows, from $22 to $1275 with a hotel.

Two houses on the yellows would still leave me broke and vulnerable to p3's light blue hotels. Three houses would threaten everyone, but I cannot afford them. No trade can give me a winning build without creating a larger threat first. p3 is the clear leader and will likely win unless I build yellow to hotel level or form an alliance to bankrupt him.

I considered building dark blue, but it is too expensive because Boardwalk is mortgaged. I also explored a trade where p1 would give me cash and Boardwalk in exchange for one of my yellows, since that would not complete his orange set. I am now considering a three-way alliance.

I cannot trade with more than one player at a time. I considered giving New York Avenue to p2, but he has no other orange properties and would likely not pay much for it. I also considered giving Park Place to p2, but he does not hold Boardwalk and it would not complete his dark blue set. I rejected any trade that would help p3.

I considered asking p1 for all four railroads plus cash in exchange for New York Avenue. He would mortgage them before trading, so I would gain the $200 per landing income but he would immediately build his orange set and kill me faster.

If p1 accepted the trade, he would mortgage his four railroads and have roughly $278 left. He could build two houses on one orange property for about $150 in rent, or one house each on two properties for about $50 each. That is not immediately lethal, but he could later raise those to three houses for roughly $450 each, which would be lethal. Orange is landed on frequently, so this remains a serious threat.

I reconsidered the trade where I would demand $478 cash plus all four railroads for New York Avenue. If I mortgage those four railroads, I would gain roughly $400 in addition to their cash, giving me about $1070 total. That is enough to build seven houses on the yellows, which would generate rents around $330 to $800 and make me competitive. They would end up with zero cash and an orange monopoly they cannot build on until they earn money.

A more realistic trade would offer New York Avenue for four railroads plus $200. p1 would keep $278 and build two houses on orange, leaving $78. I would mortgage the railroads for roughly $400, add their cash and my $192, giving me about $792 total. That would let me build five houses on the yellows, costing $750 and leaving a $42 buffer. The resulting rents would range from $110 to $360.

The two-house orange set would be a similar threat level, but p1 has a head start on building and lands there more often. I am starting from a lower house count with only $42 cash, so this race is likely lost. I will not trade or mortgage anything. The correct play is to end the turn.

Mortgaging all properties would yield roughly $867, enough to survive one light blue hotel hit but leaving yellow mortgaged and unable to build. Mortgaging only Park Place and New York Avenue plus cash still leaves only about $467, which cannot cover a $550 hotel rent. The $192 buffer is too small to absorb any light blue hotel hit.

Mortgaging one yellow property would yield roughly $597, enough to survive a light blue hotel hit but leaving the set mortgaged and unable to build until unmortgaged. Building a house would only worsen this vulnerability by reducing cash and forcing a half-price sale before any mortgage. I am now checking whether any trade could improve survival without giving another player a monopoly.

I will post a brief public message reiterating my stance: no builds, no deals, and New York Avenue and Park Place remain mine. I am now updating the analysis to reflect the current position after paying $18 in Indiana rent.

Mortgaging Park Place alone covers the $200 B&O Railroad debt, leaving about $167. Building a house first would leave only $42, forcing a house sale for $75 and still leaving an $83 shortfall. Even after mortgaging Park Place, cash would drop to roughly $92.

I am now uncertain which Community Chest p1 occupies. That position determines whether p1 can land on my yellows before my next turn.

From Kentucky Avenue, p2 can reach Indiana, Illinois, or B&O Railroad.

From Kentucky Avenue, p2 can land on my yellows with a 14 in 36 chance. That yields roughly $9 in expected rent if I have no houses. I must build evenly across the three yellows.

Building one house on Marvin Gardens yields the highest extra expected value at roughly $13.30. Ventnor follows at about $12.20, and Atlantic at about $9.80. p3 can land on my yellows from Illinois with a 10 in 36 chance, which would add roughly $13.30 to my income if I have one house on Marvin.

If p1 is on Community Chest 2, he can reach my yellows from there. He lands on Atlantic Avenue with a 3 in 36 chance and Ventnor Avenue with a 2 in 36 chance. Marvin Gardens is unreachable from that space. The extra expected value would be roughly $7.30 for Atlantic and $4.90 for Ventnor.

Community Chest 3 is too far from the yellows to threaten them. The combined extra expected value from one house on Marvin Gardens is roughly $27 to $34. That exceeds the $150 cost, so building is profitable.

I am now weighing the expected rent against the risk of having to sell a house at half price. The B&O Railroad hit remains the main danger, but I am also checking whether the Water Works utility could force a sale if I build first and land there with only $42 left.

Rolling a 6 from Indiana Avenue lands on Water Works for $60, which is unaffordable with only $42 left. Rolling a 2 hits Illinois for $24, leaving $18. Rolling a 3 hits B&O Railroad for $200, which is impossible to pay with either cash amount. Rolling a 10 lands on North Carolina, which costs $300 and is unaffordable.

Rolling a 12 from Indiana Avenue lands on Pennsylvania, which costs $28. That is affordable with either cash amount.

With $192, a roll of 3 leaves about $167 after paying the B&O Railroad debt. A roll of 6 leaves about $132 after paying Water Works. Both are manageable.

With only $42 left after building one house, a roll of 2 leaves just $18. A roll of 3 would still force bankruptcy.

I realized I can mortgage Park Place or New York Avenue to raise cash without selling my yellow house. That house would remain on the board, so I would not lose its value.

Mortgaging Park Place would leave about $17 after paying the B&O Railroad debt, so building a house is safe. I am now calculating the exact expected rent from one house on Marvin Gardens.

I am now calculating the exact expected rent from one house on Marvin Gardens. p2 from Kentucky can reach it on a roll of 8, adding roughly $13.33 in extra rent. p3 from Illinois can reach it on a roll of 6 for the same gain. p1 cannot land on Marvin from Community Chest 1 or 3, but from Community Chest 2 he could reach it with a roll of 12.

The best-case extra expected value from one house on Marvin Gardens is roughly $29. That includes about $13.33 from p2, about $13.33 from p3, and about $2.67 if p1 lands there from Community Chest 2.

Building the house costs $150 but leaves a cash buffer of only $42. The risk of needing to mortgage properties has shifted: without the house, only a roll of 3 forces a mortgage; with the house, even a roll of 3 would require selling it.

A roll of 6 from Indiana Avenue would force a mortgage to pay Water Works. Mortgaging New York Avenue would leave about $82, while mortgaging Park Place would leave about $157. A roll of 9 on Pacific Avenue leaves only $16. A roll of 12 on Pennsylvania Avenue leaves just $14. Community Chest could bring a bill such as a doctor visit for $50. The expected value of roughly $29 from one house is real money, and p3 has $1958 so the extra rent will not hurt them.

One house is a poor investment because it does not threaten anyone and drains the cash buffer. Threatening requires three houses on the yellows, which costs $1350 and is impossible with only $192. I am now considering trading New York Avenue to p1, who desperately wants it to complete his orange monopoly.

I cannot give New York Avenue to p1. He would mortgage his four railroads for $400, add his $478 cash, and build three houses on the orange set immediately. That would create a second death set worth roughly $550 each. I also cannot give Park Place to p1, because he already holds Boardwalk.

I am now weighing what assets I could trade for to fund building. The yellow set is my only monopoly, so trading it away would eliminate my build path unless I acquire another set.

p2 cannot complete any set without p3's properties, so p3 will not help me. p3 holds light blue hotels and $1958, so they have no incentive to trade. They do not own yellow, and buying my yellows would be suicidal for them. I will not sell New York Avenue to p1.

I checked whether p2 could trade with me for cash and properties to fund the yellow houses. He only has $466, which is far below the $1350 needed for three houses on the set. I also verified the exact rent values for each house level on the yellows, from $22 to $1275 with a hotel.

Two houses on the yellows would still leave me broke and vulnerable to p3's light blue hotels. Three houses would threaten everyone, but I cannot afford them. No trade can give me a winning build without creating a larger threat first. p3 is the clear leader and will likely win unless I build yellow to hotel level or form an alliance to bankrupt him.

I considered building dark blue, but it is too expensive because Boardwalk is mortgaged. I also explored a trade where p1 would give me cash and Boardwalk in exchange for one of my yellows, since that would not complete his orange set. I am now considering a three-way alliance.

I cannot trade with more than one player at a time. I considered giving New York Avenue to p2, but he has no other orange properties and would likely not pay much for it. I also considered giving Park Place to p2, but he does not hold Boardwalk and it would not complete his dark blue set. I rejected any trade that would help p3.

I considered asking p1 for all four railroads plus cash in exchange for New York Avenue. He would mortgage them before trading, so I would gain the $200 per landing income but he would immediately build his orange set and kill me faster.

If p1 accepted the trade, he would mortgage his four railroads and have roughly $278 left. He could build two houses on one orange property for about $150 in rent, or one house each on two properties for about $50 each. That is not immediately lethal, but he could later raise those to three houses for roughly $450 each, which would be lethal. Orange is landed on frequently, so this remains a serious threat.

I reconsidered the trade where I would demand $478 cash plus all four railroads for New York Avenue. If I mortgage those four railroads, I would gain roughly $400 in addition to their cash, giving me about $1070 total. That is enough to build seven houses on the yellows, which would generate rents around $330 to $800 and make me competitive. They would end up with zero cash and an orange monopoly they cannot build on until they earn money.

A more realistic trade would offer New York Avenue for four railroads plus $200. p1 would keep $278 and build two houses on orange, leaving $78. I would mortgage the railroads for roughly $400, add their cash and my $192, giving me about $792 total. That would let me build five houses on the yellows, costing $750 and leaving a $42 buffer. The resulting rents would range from $110 to $360.

The two-house orange set would be a similar threat level, but p1 has a head start on building and lands there more often. I am starting from a lower house count with only $42 cash, so this race is likely lost. I will not trade or mortgage anything. The correct play is to end the turn.

Mortgaging all properties would yield roughly $867, enough to survive one light blue hotel hit but leaving yellow mortgaged and unable to build. Mortgaging only Park Place and New York Avenue plus cash still leaves only about $467, which cannot cover a $550 hotel rent. The $192 buffer is too small to absorb any light blue hotel hit.

Mortgaging one yellow property would yield roughly $597, enough to survive a light blue hotel hit but leaving the set mortgaged and unable to build until unmortgaged. Building a house would only worsen this vulnerability by reducing cash and forcing a half-price sale before any mortgage. I am now checking whether any trade could improve survival without giving another player a monopoly.

I will post a brief public message reiterating my stance: no builds, no deals, and New York Avenue and Park Place remain mine. I am now updating the analysis to reflect the current position after paying $18 in Indiana rent.
